name: Cyclamen
lede: Cyclamen is a bright pink named for the flowering plant; Paterson calls the flower's color red, pink or reddish-purple.

sections.title: A flower name in the red list
sections.body:
Paterson defines cyclamen as the red or pink or reddish-purple color of the cyclamen flower, and his color index lists it under the reds, near [[crimson]] [1]. That is nearly all the books record; they give no date for the color.

The name is the plant's, but the origin of this swatch is undocumented [1]. We prefer to say so rather than invent a history. What can be said is that the name is a flower's, as with [[orchid]] and [[carnation]], and that Paterson's range runs from pink and red to reddish-purple [1]. Check the swatch against the real flower, since screen pinks are approximate [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our archive of 23,781 has this color covering at least 1% of its canvas, as photographed [2]. That describes this archive, not painting as a whole [2].

origin.source: Paterson, A Dictionary of Colour, p. 470
